verdict.rationale: Granola's docs say speaker tags put each participant's name above their parts of the conversation, which goes beyond the default Me/Them labels and directly addresses named attribution. However, the default transcript labels are only Me/Them, and nothing shows how speakers are diarized or matched to real names, or how accurate that is. missing for 10: documentation of the diarization and name-matching mechanism (e.g. from calendar or participant data), any availability conditions for speaker tags, and independent or hands-on corroboration of attribution accuracy.

support.subject: As a product manager, the transcript attributes words to the right named speakers (diarization plus real name matching), not just "Speaker 1/2"

citations.quote: Speaker tags show each participant's name above their parts of the conversation, giving you more detailed attribution than the default Me and Them labels.
